questions.text:
Consider the following grammar and the semantic actions to support the inherited type declaration attributes. Let [latex]X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4,X_5 \; and \; X_6[/latex] be the placeholders for the non-terminals D, T, L or [latex]L_1[/latex] in the following table:

Which one of the following are the appropriate choices for [latex]X_1,X_2,X_3 \; and \; X_4[/latex]?
questions.solution:
The type flows from T to the list L (inherited attribute):
- D [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T L: the list gets T's type [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]L.type=T.type[/latex], so [latex]X_1=L,\ X_2=T[/latex].
- L [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]L_1[/latex], id: pass the type down to [latex]L_1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]L_1.type=L.type[/latex], so [latex]X_3=L_1,\ X_4=L[/latex] (and id gets L.type).

Answer: [latex]X_1=L,X_2=T,X_3=L_1,X_4=L[/latex]

questions.text: There are n unsorted arrays: [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex]. Assume that n is odd. Each of [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex] contains n distinct elements. There are no common elements between any two arrays. The worst-case Asymptotic Notation of computing the median of the medians of [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex] is ________ .
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Median of each unsorted array of n elements (linear-time selection): [latex]O(n)[/latex] each, n arrays [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(n^2)[/latex].
- Median of those n medians: [latex]O(n)[/latex].

Total [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]. It cannot be less, because all [latex]n^2[/latex] elements must be looked at.

Answer: [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]

questions.text:
Let G be any connection, weighted, undirected graph:

I. G has a unique minimum spanning tree if no two edges of G have the same weight.
II. G has a unique minimum spanning tree if, for every cut of G, there is a unique minimum weight edge crossing the cut.

Which of the above two statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: with distinct weights, Kruskal never faces a tie, so the MST is unique [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- II: if every cut has a unique lightest crossing edge, the cut property forces that edge into every MST; this fixes the whole MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.text: Consider the following snapshot of a system running n concurrent processes. Process [latex]i[/latex] is holding [latex]X_i[/latex] instances of a resource R, [latex] 1\leq i\leq n[/latex]. Assume that all instances of R are currently in use. Further, for all [latex]i[/latex], process [latex]i[/latex] can place a request for at most [latex]Y_i[/latex] additional instances of R while holding the [latex]X_i[/latex] instances it already has. Of the n processes, there are exactly two processes p and q such that [latex]Y_p=Y_q=0[/latex]. Which one of the following conditions guarantees that no other process apart from p and q can complete execution?
questions.solution:
p and q need nothing more, so they finish and release [latex]X_p+X_q[/latex] instances (all others are in use).

Any other process k can finish only if it gets [latex]Y_k[/latex] instances. If [latex]X_p+X_q \lt \min_k Y_k[/latex], the freed instances are not enough for any other process, so none of them can complete.

Answer: [latex]X_p+X_q \lt Min\{Y_k\}[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:

I. The smallest element in a max-heap is always at a leaf node.
II. The second largest element in a max-heap is always a child of the root node.
III. A max-heap can be constructed from a binary search tree in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time.
IV. A binary search tree can be constructed from a max-heap in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: a node with a child is larger than that child, so the minimum has no child [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] it is a leaf [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- II: the 2nd largest can only be smaller than the root, so its parent must be the root [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- III: build-heap on any array (e.g. the BST's elements) takes [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- IV: a BST from a heap in [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] would give an [latex]O(n)[/latex] comparison sort (inorder traversal) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: I, II and III
